title: Prevention of coronary heart disease with pravastatin in men with hypercholesterolemia
authors: Shepherd J, Cobbe SM, Ford I, Isles CG, Lorimer AR, MacFarlane PW, et al.
population: Men aged 45 to 64 years in the West of Scotland with mean plasma cholesterol 7.0 mmol/L and LDL cholesterol 5.0 mmol/L and no history of myocardial infarction (West of Scotland Coronary Prevention Study, WOSCOPS)
funder: Supported by a research grant from the Bristol-Myers Squibb Pharmaceutical Research Institute, Princeton, N.J.
result: Double-blind pravastatin 40 mg each evening against placebo. Pravastatin lowered plasma cholesterol by 20% and LDL cholesterol by 26%. Definite coronary events (non-fatal myocardial infarction or death from coronary heart disease): 248 with placebo and 174 with pravastatin, relative risk reduction 31% (95% CI 17 to 43; P < 0.001), absolute difference in 5-year risk 2.4 percentage points. Death from any cause 22% lower (0 to 40; P = 0.051). Authors' estimate per 1000 men treated for 5 years: 20 fewer non-fatal myocardial infarctions, 7 fewer deaths from cardiovascular causes and 2 fewer deaths from other causes.
